title: Multithreading and Concurrency in Java
description: Understand concurrent execution in Java and learn to build reliable, thread-safe applications. Cover thread creation and lifecycle, Runnable and Callable, synchronization, race conditions, deadlocks, and thread safety. Explore ExecutorService, CompletableFuture, concurrent collections, and atomic variables through practical examples.

topics.title: Thread Fundamentals, Creation and Lifecycle
topics.description: Understand Java threads, their lifecycle, and the different ways to create and manage concurrent tasks.
subtopics: Thread methods: sleep, join, interrupt, and yield

topics.title: Callable, Future and Task Execution
topics.description: Execute tasks that return results and handle asynchronous task completion using Java concurrency APIs.

topics.title: Synchronization, Race Conditions and Thread Safety
topics.description: Understand problems caused by shared mutable data and apply synchronization techniques to protect critical sections.

topics.title: Deadlocks and Concurrent Programming Problems
topics.description: Identify common concurrency problems and learn practical techniques to prevent deadlocks and unsafe thread interactions.

topics.title: ExecutorService and Thread Pool Management
topics.description: Manage concurrent tasks efficiently using executor services and reusable thread pools instead of creating threads manually.
subtopics: Fixed, cached, single-thread, and scheduled thread pools

topics.title: Concurrent Collections and Atomic Variables
topics.description: Use thread-safe data structures and atomic operations to coordinate access to shared data in concurrent applications.
subtopics: Limitations of standard collections during concurrent access

topics.title: Asynchronous Programming with CompletableFuture
topics.description: Build asynchronous workflows by composing tasks, combining results, and handling errors using CompletableFuture.
subtopics: CompletableFuture and its relationship with Future
Combining tasks with thenCombine() and allOf()
Handling exceptions with exceptionally() and handle()

topics.title: Concurrency Best Practices and Practical Scenarios
topics.description: Apply concurrency concepts to realistic Java scenarios and choose appropriate tools for reliable concurrent application design.
subtopics: Choosing between synchronized and concurrent utilities
Choosing threads, thread pools, and asynchronous tasks
Avoiding shared mutable state where possible
Common concurrency mistakes and debugging approaches
